newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan may drop support for a proposed submarine pipeline project to import gas from Qatar in favour of a land pipeline to be built by Iran, Sartaj Aziz, Pakistan's Finance Minister said.
- Sharjah city was almost paralysed as people tried to make the most of the water left in their tanks after an oil spill caused a shutdown of a desalination plant.
- Tyre piece on Dubai International airport runway sparks alerts at airports.
- Qatar may call off Middle East and North Africa (MENA) summit.
- UAE employers to report twice a year on job vacancies.
- Water supply in Sharjah may resume today.
- Short term returns on Saudi stocks average 23 percent.
- Dubai bans advertising boards on balconies.
- Onshore oil production of the divided zone between Kuwait and Saudi Arabia has gone up to 240,000 barrels a day following resumption of production from al-Wafra oilfield, an oil bulletin said.
- Gulf Cooperation Council states are committed to reduce spending and boost revenues from taxes, an Arab Banking Corporation study said.
